text: Experiment zero two: Continuity tester. In this experiment, we check if there is continuity between two points and learn about open circuits.
The components required are: a three-volt battery ePod, a red LED ePod, three jump wires, and two single-strand wires.
Here is the circuit diagram from the workbook. Battery positive connects to LED positive. The negative terminals connect to two single-strand wires that serve as testing probes.
Let us build the circuit. Connect battery positive to LED positive with a jump wire. Then attach single-strand wires to the battery negative and LED negative terminals, leaving two open testing ends.
When the open ends do not touch each other, the LED does not glow. This is an open circuit, because electricity cannot flow through the air.
Now, touch the two open ends directly together. The LED glows immediately! Touching the ends completes the circuit, allowing electric current to flow.
Next, place the open ends on a metal steel ring. The LED glows brightly! Metals are good conductors of electricity and allow electric current to pass through them.
Now, test with a piece of paper. The LED does not glow, because paper is a bad conductor, or insulator. Testing on a plastic box also keeps the LED off, because plastic is an insulator.
To summarize: an open circuit has an incomplete path so the LED stays off. A closed circuit has a complete conducting path, allowing current to flow and lighting the LED.
